clue.text: King is going to home in Hungarian Germany, sorting place for 12

indicators.note: in tells us the king, the future tense and home go inside the word for Hungarian

parts.note: a Magyar is a Hungarian
R, for rex, is the usual abbreviation for king
shall expresses the future, like is going to
at home is in
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A king plans to settle in a Hungarian part of Germany, somewhere good for sorting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is RAIL, so the definition describes a yard where railway wagons are sorted into trains; Germany gives its vehicle code, not a German word.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshalling yard is where railway wagons are sorted and assembled into trains.

clue.text: Second XI's crazy driver, veteran on 12

parts.note: a team of eleven players, as in cricket or football, is an XI
loco is slang for crazy
a motive is what drives someone to act

explanation.surface: The second eleven has a mad captain, an old hand who rides the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is RAIL, so a 'veteran on rail' is an old-fashioned engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam engines are the old-timers of the railway, largely replaced by diesel and electric traction.

clue.text: Possibly second century termination to stoop

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way, signalling an anagram

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century (Roman numeral 100)
a termination is an end

explanation.surface: Perhaps the second century saw the end of bowing low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges SECOND plus C into CONDESC, and END finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to lower oneself, to stoop to something beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Boy restricts comedian to point on 12

indicators.note: restricts means the word for boy hems in, or encloses, the comedian

parts.note: a son is a boy
Jacques Tati was a French comic actor and film-maker

explanation.surface: A lad keeps a comic in check on a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is RAIL, so a point on the rail is a stopping place.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway station is a stopping point along the line.

clue.text: Set aside part of the laws of cricket?

definitions.text: part of the laws of cricket?

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: the laws of cricket include a rule about the over, a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule a decision is to set it aside using higher authority.

clue.text: Major House of Lords account pin revealed by busy 4

indicators.note: the letters are jumbled and then revealed as something else, a loose anagram signal

parts.note: Maj is the abbreviation for the military rank of major
HL is the abbreviation for the House of Lords
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior officer's account in the Lords is exposed by a bustling station.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is STATION. Clapham Junction in south London is often called Britain's busiest railway station. 'revealed by' is a loose anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham Junction in London is famous as one of the busiest railway interchanges in Britain.

clue.text: Dr Martin Luther in trauma, first in anger, no longer available on 12

indicators.note: in places the doctor and the civil rights leader inside the wound

parts.note: a scar is the mark of a trauma or injury
MO, medical officer, is a doctor
Martin Luther King, the American civil rights leader

indicators.note: in#2 puts the numeral for first inside the word for anger

parts.note: rage is anger
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: A doctor called Martin Luther, caught up in trauma and seething, is no longer to be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr' is MO and 'Martin Luther' gives KING, not the Protestant reformer. Railway compartments for smokers were abolished, hence no longer available on the rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking carriages were railway coaches set aside for smokers, now abolished on British trains.

clue.text: No more letters after the bugler's farewell

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the final mail collection of the day; the other is the bugle call played at military funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The final collection of mail is the last one, and the bugle call sounded at dusk and at funerals has the same name.

clue.text: How big is the book?

explanation.definitionFit: Volume means size or capacity, and also a single bound book in a set.

clue.text: Middle of the road, like Britain?

explanation.walkthrough: A traffic island sits in the middle of a road; Britain is surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic refuge in the roadway and a landmass surrounded by water share the name.

clue.text: Tailless bird accepts changing pin will take its toll

indicators.note: accepts means the shortened bird takes the rearranged letters into itself
tailless means the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a turkey is a bird

indicators.note: changing tells us the three letters of pin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail takes in a shifting pin and suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will take its toll' plays on the idiom for causing damage over time: a turnpike literally collects tolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike was a road with gates where travellers paid a toll to pass.

clue.text: Scoff at bird on land or water

explanation.walkthrough: The bird family includes the water rail and the landrail (corncrake).
explanation.definitionFit: To rail at is to complain bitterly or mock, and the rail is a family of marsh birds.

clue.text: Stoppers on 12 forming 2 12s on poles

indicators.note: forming signals that the pieces are reshaped into a new word

parts.note: the figure is written out as a word
the answer to 12 across, pluralised
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Things that halt, shaped like a pair of tracks between the poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is RAIL. 'forming' rearranges TWO RAILS plus N and S. Stoppers here means trains that call at every station.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow trains are stopping services that call at every station on the line.

clue.text: Lack of practice demands time before achieving reliability

indicators.note: before puts the abbreviation for time at the front

parts.note: a skill unused grows rusty, so lack of practice is rustiness

explanation.surface: Being out of practice demands time before you become dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Trustiness is the quality of being trustworthy, a near synonym of dependability.

clue.text: Light on movie queen?

parts.note: a flick is a movie
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A light shines on a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movie queen' looks like a star; split it into a film and a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A flicker is a brief unsteady light, such as a candle gives.

clue.text: Inferior theme

explanation.definitionFit: Subject means under another's authority, and also the topic of a discussion.

clue.text: Looks to finish letter

explanation.definitionFit: Regards are looks or glances, and the word is a common sign-off at the end of a letter.

clue.text: Comment on an individual and very angry Green

parts.note: I is the single person, an individual
mad means very angry
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Remarks about a person who is furious and environmentally minded.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic term for green. 'Green' looks like an environmental campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert on something is to criticise or remark on it, usually disapprovingly.

clue.text: Fiddler for one roof

indicators.note: for here means the clue words provide the letters, which sit within them

explanation.surface: A fiddler, say, on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the musical Fiddler on the Roof; the Roman emperor was said to fiddle while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor Nero is said to have played the fiddle while Rome burned.

clue.text: This year's problem is out of control

indicators.note: out of control means the letters run wild and land in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: This year's difficulty is getting out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is a state of uncontrolled panic or emotion, a problem of the mind.

clue.text: See 5
Crazy tune backed by furry invader

parts.note: nuts or a nut means crazy

indicators.note: backed means the word for tune is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A mad song accompanies an invasive furry creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns AIR into RIA. The nutria, or coypu, is a large South American rodent that became an invasive pest in Britain and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutria (coypu) is a furry rodent that has spread invasively outside its native South America.

clue.text: Top piece missing, composer might go by 12

indicators.note: missing tells us a piece is taken out of the word top

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical piece
Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: With the top part gone, a composer could take the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes OP (a musical work) from TOP, leaving T. 12 across is RAIL, so to go by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to make a journey, here by rail.

clue.text: Pour out from the throat of hell?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, hence hell
gorge is an old word for the throat

explanation.surface: Spewing forth from the mouth of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgorge is to discharge or eject contents, as from the throat.
